Cc: legal@tilecorp.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood order form — a few IP questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending over the latest order form. Our legal team surfaced two short items they want clarified before procurement signs:

1) Output ownership: TileCorp needs confirmation that outputs (generated text derived from our prompts/data) are owned by us for our internal use and for embedding into our product.
2) Training/feedback license: the draft currently grants Redwood a perpetual feedback license to use customer inputs/outputs to improve models. We need this scoped: internal analytics/ops okay, but no right to train models used by others on unredacted TileCorp data.

I've attached our redlines (TileCorp_Redlines_v2.docx). Can we get proposed compromise language from Redwood legal? If easier, we can hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Ben Jacobs
Director of Platform Partnerships
TileCorp

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redlines. Karthik and I reviewed and looped in Priyom (contracts) to propose compromise language. Quick answers up front: we can accept customer ownership of outputs for your internal use and product embedding, and we can narrow the feedback license so it does not grant the right to train models on identifiable TileCorp data used in production.

That said, we need workable language that preserves Redwood's ability to:
- Use anonymized, aggregated telemetry to improve service reliability and model safety;
- Use high-level feedback signals (e.g., anonymized mislabeled cases, utility metrics) for commercial model improvements, absent identifiable customer data.

I'll attach a redline of the order form with suggested wording. Can we do a 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize? Karthik — do you have availability 9:30-11am PT?

Best,

Ben / Priya —

Thanks — following Priya's note, Priyom and I drafted compromise text that aligns with our standard playbook while addressing TileCorp's concerns. High-level summary of the proposed approach:

1) Output ownership: TileCorp retains ownership of outputs you submit and receive ("Customer Outputs") for your internal business purposes and to incorporate into your products; Redwood receives a limited, non-exclusive right to store and cache Customer Outputs for debugging, telemetry, and to provide the service.

2) Training/Feedback license: Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and feedback derived from Customer Outputs to improve the Redwood platform, provided such data is not reasonably capable of re-identifying TileCorp or its end users. Redwood will not use unredacted Customer Inputs or Customer Outputs to train public or commercial models that are served to third parties.

3) Audit & safeguards: add commitments to (a) data minimization during telemetry collection, (b) option for TileCorp to request sandboxing/segregation for particularly sensitive workloads, and (c) SOC 2 / contractual security controls already in the MSA.

Draft language is pasted below and in the attached redline (see Article 5, Terms re: "Customer Data and Use"). If that looks ok, Karthik and I can turn this into an updated order form for signature.

--- Proposed clause (excerpt) ---
"Customer Outputs: Customer owns all intellectual property rights in and to Customer Outputs. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to store, cache, and process Customer Outputs solely to provide the Services, troubleshoot incidents, and perform aggregated analytics.

Feedback & Training: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry and feedback derived from Customer Outputs for the purpose of improving the Services, provided Redwood shall not use unredacted Customer Inputs or Customer Outputs to train models that are served to or sold to third parties without Customer's explicit written consent. Redwood will implement and maintain industry-standard de-identification techniques and data minimization consistent with its SOC 2 controls."

--- end excerpt ---

Ping me with any redline suggestions. If TileCorp prefers a carveout path (e.g., buy-down to allow Redwood to use feedback for internal research but not production models) we can draft that.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — and thanks Priya.

This proposed language addresses the main concerns from TileCorp legal. A couple of small asks before we proceed to signature: 

1) Can we add an explicit definition of "de-identified" that references removal of direct identifiers and a prohibition on re-identification attempts without Customer consent?
2) For particularly sensitive datasets (we'll flag them at contract execution), TileCorp wants the option to require isolated model tuning (i.e., models fine-tuned only on our data in a sandbox) for an additional fee — can Redwood add a short clause referencing a "sandboxed tuning" addendum?

If you can include those two items in a final draft we can route to procurement and legal to sign off. Happy to approve once those edits are in.

Best,
